principles: Single source of truth: one typed ledger map; toFindingAddArgs is the only place an abstract severity becomes a finding_add severity.
Structural no-abstract-leak: the compiler + the map guarantee finding_add never sees BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR.
Threshold-confirm, not majority: CONFIRMED iff confirms>=T (default T=1-of-2); refute-by-default counts only isReal===true.
Hermetic + injected: the skeptic is a (finding,change)=>Verdict seam; the module counts+thresholds, the role refutes.
Stay inside S2: verify + map only; no lens runner (S1), no critic (S3), no finding_add/escalation I/O (S4).
drivers: finding_add enum is critical|high|medium|low — an abstract severity is a Zod error (§4.2).
§2.3 fixes refute-by-default + threshold-confirm default T=1-of-2 (explicitly not majority).
S0 contract (Finding/FindingSeverity/Verdict) is frozen and imported verbatim; S1/S3/S4 are out of scope.

options.name: Injected-skeptic verifier + const ledger map + pure arg-builder
pros: The skeptic is an injected (finding,change)=>Verdict seam so the module is hermetically testable with a fake; refute-by-default lives in the skeptic role, the module only counts isReal and thresholds (single responsibility)

SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND is a typed const Record<FindingSeverity, FindingAddSeverity> so the compiler forces a mapping for every abstract severity and toFindingAddArgs can never emit BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR (prevents the Zod error structurally)
T and M are parameters (defaults T=1,M=2) so the precision/recall tradeoff is tunable per §2.3; pure functions, no I/O, so finding_add stays S4
cons: The real skeptic agent is not wired here (deferred to S4) so MVP value is a library seam + mapping, not an end-to-end finding_add

options.name: Verifier computes severity strings inline at the finding_add call site
cons: No single source of truth for the BLOCKER->critical map; each call site can drift or forget to map and hit the Zod error
Cannot prove the no-abstract-leak property hermetically
Couples mapping to I/O — crosses into S4

options.name: Bake majority voting into the verifier instead of threshold-confirm
cons: Contradicts §2.3 which is explicitly NOT majority: with M=2 a majority needs 2 confirms but the spec default is T=1-of-2 (one concrete proof suffices)
Would drop real defects only one skeptic can see — the opposite of the intended safety bias
Not tunable to the precision end (T=2-of-2) the spec requires

chosen: Injected-skeptic verifier + const ledger map + pure arg-builder
rationale: Only this option satisfies all five principles: a typed const map that structurally prevents the abstract-severity Zod error, a pure arg-builder that keeps finding_add I/O in S4, and an injected skeptic seam with confirms>=T threshold-confirm (default 1-of-2) that is hermetically testable and matches §2.3 exactly. The inline-at-call-site option loses the single-source-of-truth + no-leak proof; the majority-vote option directly contradicts §2.3.

preMortem.scenario: An abstract methodology severity (BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR) reaches finding_add and triggers a Zod enum error at runtime
preMortem.trigger: A caller composes finding_add args by hand or toFindingAddArgs passes finding.severity through unmapped
preMortem.consequence: S4 escalation calls finding_add with an invalid severity and the finding is rejected — a real confirmed defect is silently lost from the ledger
preMortem.mitigation: SEVERITY_TO_FINDING_KIND is a typed Record<FindingSeverity, 'critical'|'high'|'medium'|'low'>; toFindingAddArgs ONLY emits the mapped value; the smoke asserts every emitted severity is in {critical,high,medium,low} and never equals an abstract severity

preMortem.scenario: The threshold is implemented as a majority vote instead of confirms>=T, so T=1-of-2 behaves like T=2-of-2
preMortem.trigger: verifyFinding uses confirms > M/2 (majority) rather than confirms >= T
preMortem.consequence: A real defect that only one of two skeptics concretely confirms is dropped — the review loses recall exactly where §2.3 says it must not
preMortem.mitigation: verifyFinding uses confirmed = (confirms >= threshold) with default threshold=1; the smoke plants a fake giving 1 isReal of 2 and asserts CONFIRMED under T=1, and DROPPED under T=2, pinning threshold-confirm (not majority)

preMortem.scenario: Refute-by-default is silently inverted — a skeptic that returns no clear verdict is counted as a confirmation
preMortem.trigger: verifyFinding counts isReal !== false (treating undefined/missing as confirm) instead of isReal === true
preMortem.consequence: Confident-but-wrong findings survive (confirms inflated), defeating the single failure mode §2.3 exists to filter
preMortem.mitigation: confirms counts strictly v.isReal === true; a confirms=0 finding is dropped; the smoke includes a fake that returns isReal=false for all skeptics and asserts the finding is DROPPED, and a mixed case asserting only true verdicts count
